an4.21:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
an4.21:1.3: There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus:
an4.21:2.1: “Bhikkhus, on one occasion I was dwelling at Uruvelā, by the goatherds’ banyan tree on the bank of the Neranjarā River, just after I had attained full enlightenment.
an4.21:2.2: Then, while I was alone in seclusion, a course of thought arose in my mind thus:
an4.21:2.3: ‘It is painful to dwell without reverence and deference.
an4.21:2.4: Now what ascetic or brahmin can I honor, respect, and dwell in dependence on?’
an4.21:3.2: (1) ‘If my aggregate of virtuous behavior were incomplete, for the sake of completing it I would honor, respect, and dwell in dependence on another ascetic or brahmin.
an4.21:3.3: However, in this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, among this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, I do not see another ascetic or brahmin more accomplished in virtuous behavior than myself whom I could honor, respect, and dwell in dependence on.
an4.21:4.1: (2) “‘If my aggregate of concentration were incomplete, for the sake of completing it I would honor, respect, and dwell in dependence on another ascetic or brahmin.
an4.21:4.2: However … I do not see another ascetic or brahmin more accomplished in concentration than myself….
an4.21:5.1: (3) “‘If my aggregate of wisdom were incomplete, for the sake of completing it I would honor, respect, and dwell in dependence on another ascetic or brahmin.
an4.21:5.2: However … I do not see another ascetic or brahmin more accomplished in wisdom than myself….
an4.21:6.1: (4) “‘If my aggregate of liberation were incomplete, for the sake of completing it I would honor, respect, and dwell in dependence on another ascetic or brahmin.
an4.21:6.2: However, in this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, among this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, I do not see another ascetic or brahmin more accomplished in liberation than myself whom I could honor, respect, and dwell in dependence on.
an4.21:7.2: ‘Let me then honor, respect, and dwell in dependence only on this Dhamma to which I have become fully enlightened.’
an4.21:8.1: “Then Brahmā Sahampati, having known with his own mind the reflection in my mind, disappeared from the brahmā world and reappeared before me just as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm.
an4.21:8.2: He arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, bent down with his right knee on the ground, reverently saluted me, and said:
an4.21:8.3: ‘So it is, Blessed One! So it is, Fortunate One!
an4.21:8.4: Bhante, those who were the Arahants, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the past—those Blessed Ones, too, honored, respected, and dwelled in dependence only on the Dhamma.
an4.21:8.5: Those who will be the Arahants, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the future—those Blessed Ones, too, will honor, respect, and dwell in dependence only on the Dhamma.
an4.21:8.6: Let the Blessed One, too, who is at present the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, honor, respect, and dwell in dependence only on the Dhamma.’
an4.21:8.8: Having said this, he further said this:
an4.21:9.4: who removes the sorrow of many:
an4.21:10.3: and in the future will dwell
an4.21:10.4:
revering the good Dhamma.
This is the nature of the Buddhas.
an4.21:12.2: He then paid homage to me, and keeping me on his right, he disappeared right there.
an4.21:12.3: Then, having acknowledged Brahmā’s request and what was proper for myself, I honored, respected, and dwelled in dependence only on the Dhamma to which I had become fully enlightened.
an4.21:12.4: And now that the Saṅgha has acquired greatness, I have respect for the Saṅgha, too.”
